provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
Constructor: the canvas is exactly 7 wide and 6-12 tall, with no extras in fresh scenes. Its marker cells (colour 4) sit on the canvas border at both ends of every line, plus at some interior crossings. Lines never sit on the canvas border rows or columns (spaces are at least 1), so the bounding box of colour 4 is exactly the output canvas and its corners are never markers.

The legend is the background rectangle inside the grey (5) block, of size (2H+1)x(2V+1). Its vertical lines sit at odd columns and span every legend row; its horizontal lines sit at odd rows and span every legend column. So the bounding box of line colours is exactly that rectangle. Its first row lists the vertical-line colours and its first column lists the horizontal-line colours.

The legend and the output are drawn in the same shuffled order. So each legend crossing cell is exactly the output crossing colour. Line positions (ivals and ovals) increase together, so pairing the k-th marker line with the k-th legend line in visible order is correct. Any reflection or flop reverses both orders at once, so the pairing still holds.

The whole mechanism treats rows and columns the same way and does not depend on which corner holds the legend. Under any D4 transform it therefore stays correct in visible coordinates without rotating anything. Visible vertical lines are read from the top and bottom box edges; visible horizontal lines are read from the left and right edges.

Colour roles are fixed constants: background = palette[0], marker = palette[4], frame = palette[5]. The line colours are read from the legend pixels. d4 does not need to change the code because the rule is equivariant under D4.
draft_notes.limitations: Not tested by me. Assumes palette is a permutation, so palette[0], palette[4] and palette[5] are distinct from the line colours palette[1..3]. If marker and legend line counts ever differed, zip would truncate; the constructor never produces that. The approved test fixture uses the constructor's erows/egrids extras: it changes two legend crossing cells and the matching output cells. These changes stay consistent with the crossing-cell rule, so they are handled, but fresh generate() calls never produce them. There is also a minor indexing oddity: ecols has five entries for four erows, and zip silently drops the extra. This does not affect outputs but should be noted for host review. No fixture contradicts the uniform rule.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The legend is the bounding box of non-background, non-marker, non-frame colours. Its first row gives the vertical-line colours at odd offsets, and its first column gives the horizontal-line colours. The output canvas is the bounding box of the marker colour. Visible vertical lines are the interior columns with a marker on the top or bottom box edge. Visible horizontal lines are the interior rows with a marker on the left or right edge. The k-th canvas line pairs with the k-th legend line on each axis. Each output crossing copies the legend's crossing cell, which encodes the draw order.
evidence: Both line counts are at least 1: verts = randint(1,3) and horizs = randint(1,2). Every vertical line puts markers at r==0 and r+1==height, and every horizontal line puts markers at c==0 and c+1==width. So the marker bounding box is always the full 7 x height canvas.

Every space is at least 1, including the popped last space. So line ovals lie in [1, W-2] and [1, H-2]. Edge markers therefore occur only at true line positions, and box corners are never markers. The solver's range(1, W-1) and range(1, H-1) are safe.
Interior markers come from `output[r][oval] != 0` and only fall at crossing positions. Crossings are never on box edges, so they cannot create false entries in vcols or hrows.

The legend rectangle is (2*verts+1) x (2*horizs+1). Vertical lines fill odd columns over all legend rows, and horizontal lines fill odd rows over all legend columns. The colour bounding box is therefore exactly this rectangle. Row 0 and column 0 are never crossing cells, so lv and lh are exactly the line positions, and the extras (which touch only odd,odd cells) cannot disturb them.
Legend and output are drawn in the same shuffled loop. Each crossing cell in both takes the colour of whichever line was drawn later, so leg[lr,lc] equals out[r,c].

On each axis, ival and oval both increase with i, so visible order pairs them correctly. Flop and any D4 transform act on the whole grid. Reversals flip both orders together and transposes swap both axes together, and odd offsets stay odd under reversal of an odd length. The pairing therefore holds in visible coordinates.

In the test fixture, the extras set grid[1][3]=3 and grid[3][3]=2. The matching output cells are output[4][3]=3 (row ival1 maps to oval4, column ival3 maps to oval3) and output[9][3]=2 (row ival3 maps to oval9). These agree with the crossing-cell rule, and the listed test output matches.

The solver uses only palette-mapped role constants (palette[0], palette[4], palette[5]) and reads line colours from the legend. It needs no learned colour association and does not untransform the grid. The host audit passed 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks and 16 fixture variants.
nonblocking_limits: Assumes palette is a permutation, so the background, marker and frame colours stay distinct from the line colours palette[1..3].
zip would silently truncate if the marker and legend line counts differed. The constructor always makes them equal because ovals are distinct and spaced.
The early returns (no marker, or no legend colour) are out-of-domain fallbacks that the constructor never triggers.

The extra legend crossing overrides (erows/egrids) appear only in the approved test fixture, never in fresh generation. ecols has 5 entries for 4 erows; zip drops the extra, and outputs are unaffected.
Accept means no blocking source issue was found. It does not prove correctness on inputs outside the constructor's domain.
